text.text_excerpt: While there are a couple places around town for good pizza, Ancora is the most authentic Italian style that I've come across. The pizzas are simple, and they let the ingredients speak for themselves. Love the beautiful brick oven by the bar. The restaurant has a nice space, and it is always busy, but I've never had to wait more than 15 minutes to get a table. After they first opened, I was here constantly. I may have even gone three times in one week just because I was so excited to share it with different friends. The pizza is delicious and not too doughy. Get the Diavolo, it is spicy and full of flavor. The bruschetta is good too, the bread they use is amazing. I've also enjoyed the sal...

The more I think about Ancora, the more I really liked it. I am not a pizza snob, more of a pizza slob. We tend to order Papa's once a week and break out the Tabasco, homegrown banana peppers, and ranch, yes I defile my pizzas with a ton of ranch. Back to Ancora...We were going to get it to go so we could marathon watch American Horror Story's The Coven, but I begged that we stay in and eat. The space is expansive, with a great big window similar to other businesses on Freret. We received our menus and the beer menu, were told specials were on the wall, and left to decide. We were kinda hangry, so after deciding, we're like, "yo where'd our buddy waiter go?" but I think it was the hunger ...

Two recent visits to Ancora have me hooked! The service has been consistently 5 stars. I love all the food I've eaten there too. My hands down fav drink there is the Kalimocho(sp?) cocktail with red wine and I *think* Italian cola. Sorta like a bitter sangria vibe, it's so good I can't branch out and try something else. I suggest ordering a few apps and then splitting pizza. For the 3 of us, 3 apps and one pizza were plenty! The beurre gnocchi is buttery and light and made from scratch- the best gnocchi I've ever eaten.
